subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, ACME Product Team <product-eval@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Samantha - great to meet today, thanks for the time and for walking the team through the main integration and latency targets. Quick recap and the next steps I promised: 

1) Recap of what you told us:
- Primary use case: in-product conversational assistant + short-form summarization for customer support tickets (avg. 160 tokens request, 60 token responses).
- SLOs: 99th pct latency under 350ms for chat flows, throughput ~50 rps during peak.
- Constraints: strict PII handling, on-cloud (no on-prem), strong emphasis on deterministic output quality for compliance.

2) What we agreed I'd send:
- Shortlist of recommended model variants with rationale (cost / latency / quality tradeoffs)
- Benchmark links and our prompt set used for evaluation
- Proposed next steps and a mutual action plan for a 2-week POC

I'm attaching the prompt set we used and will follow up with a benchmark summary. High-level shortlist below - will send the full scorecard in the next message so you can share with the technical team.

Recommended shortlist (initial):
- redwood-rlhf-7b-q4 (balanced): best fit if you want a strong quality/latency balance at lower cost; good for summarization and most chat prompts.
- opentrove-13b-int8 (higher quality): more accurate on instruction-following and factuality, higher latency/cost - consider for high-risk content.
- tiny-lama-3b-llm (low-latency): excellent tail latency and cost for high-concurrency, but slightly weaker on long-form factual accuracy.

Next steps:
- I'll send the benchmark CSV and a short model scorecard by tomorrow.
- If this shortlist looks reasonable, suggest a 2-week POC: 1 week benching with your prompt set + 1 week integration test with a small subset of production traffic.

Thanks - talk soon.

 - 
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v1.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>

Cc: ACME Product Team <product-eval@acme.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Thanks Marissa - helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we pick models to bench: 

- Can you share quantitative numbers for avg latency (p50/p95/p99) and token cost for the three candidates using our prompt set?
- Factuality/regression: last time we tested a similarly sized model we saw a notable increase in hallucinations on long-form summaries. Do you have examples of failure modes or mitigations (prompt engineering, reranking, brief eval outputs)?
- Security/compliance: since we're sending PII-containing tickets, will the hosted API provide masked logs or options to avoid storing raw content?

If you can provide a short scorecard + sample outputs and the benchmark CSV that would help the technical team. We're aiming to finalize which models to bring into the POC by EOD Friday.

 - 
Samantha Lee
Head of AI Products | Acme Corp
Samantha.Lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, ACME Product Team <product-eval@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Samantha - great questions, and exactly the right things to validate before the POC. I've attached the benchmark summary and model scorecard (high level) so you can review with the team. Below are the key datapoints and mitigations.

Attached: acme_benchmark_summary_20260709.csv, redwood_model_scorecard.pdf

High-level performance (using your prompt set; 160 input / 60 output token profile):
- redwood-rlhf-7b-q4 (balanced): p50=120ms, p95=280ms, p99=420ms; token cost est = $0.0018 / 1k tokens. Quality: strong on concise summaries and instruction following; low hallucination rate in our eval (1.8% factual errors on the test set).
- opentrove-13b-int8 (higher quality): p50=210ms, p95=420ms, p99=650ms; token cost est = $0.0042 / 1k tokens. Quality: best factuality (0.9% errors) and instruction adherence; higher latency and cost.
- tiny-lama-3b-llm (low-latency): p50=95ms, p95=180ms, p99=300ms; token cost est = $0.0011 / 1k tokens. Quality: good for short answers and high concurrency but shows a higher long-form error rate (3.6% on summaries).

Notes on hallucination/regression and mitigations:
- Prompt engineering: we include explicit system prompts with guidelines and citation style; examples included in attached prompt_set PDF.
- Reranking/verification: for high-risk summaries we recommend a lightweight factual verifier (we can enable a rerank step using embeddings similarity to the ticket content).
- Guardrails: Redwood Hosted offers options to disable raw input logging and provide redacted logs for audit. We can also set data retention to meet your policy - I'll link you to the security questionnaire.

Recommended approach for the POC (my suggestion):
- Primary candidate: redwood-rlhf-7b-q4 (starts default POC)
- Secondary candidate: opentrove-13b-int8 (if you need stronger factuality for a high-risk subset)
- Canary low-latency mode: tiny-lama-3b-llm for high-throughput non-sensitive paths

Next steps I propose:
- I'll open a HubSpot deal update (link below) and share the Drive folder with scorecards and raw CSVs.
- If you approve, we'll provision a 2-week POC (sample config below) and schedule a 30-min kickoff next Tuesday to sync with your infra team.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2026-07-01
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-evals

Attachment stubs: acme_benchmark_summary_20260709.csv (CSV, 18KB), redwood_model_scorecard.pdf (PDF, 24KB)

 - 
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

- On the compliance side: can we enable redaction + no raw log retention for ACME (they'll need a written statement we can include in the SOW).

I've added the HubSpot deal id: ACME-2026-07-01. ACME wants model-level p99 numbers and a security confirmation by EOD Monday so they can decide on the POC.

Thanks - propose we sync Monday AM if you need to align on implementation details.

Marissa
